source_policy.allowed_sources: Official current institution catalogs and official institution policy or organizational pages only. An explicitly labeled historical Sweet Briar news page is retained solely to explain a stale-program false positive and is not used as current degree evidence.
source_policy.selection_rule: Preserve the catalog's exact award and variant structure. Do not merge BA and BS awards, optional concentrations, required emphasis variants, accelerated options, or recommended schedules into a single base degree.
source_policy.unknown_rule: A null constraint means no current official numeric requirement was found in the reviewed sources; it must not be interpreted as zero. Computed totals are labeled computed and are not represented as published totals.

institutions.name: Ferrum College

degree.selection_evidence: The current Programs by Degree index publishes no unqualified Computer Science B.S. It publishes four separately named emphasis awards, all with a 36-credit shared core, 24 emphasis credits, 60 program credits, and 120 degree credits. Selecting one as the standard program requires a product/research policy decision rather than a source inference.

owner.evidence: Ferrum's current official directory assigns the Computer Science faculty member to the School of Sciences and Agriculture. No separate current Computer Science department was found in the reviewed catalog or official organizational pages.

major_requirements.evidence: There is no single current base-program page. The four authoritative variant URLs are retained in degree.published_variants and must not be collapsed.

exclude_from_base_requirements.reason: They are prospective schedules, not the categorical catalog requirement authority.

general_education.evidence: The current catalog states that the 30-credit General Education Curriculum is required of all Ferrum College graduates and divides it into Common Competencies and Discipline Competencies.

total_credits.evidence: Each of the four current Computer Science B.S. variant pages explicitly publishes 120 total degree credits.

upper_division.evidence: The current transfer policy says students must meet the number of upper-level hours required by the major and College, but it does not publish an aggregate numeric minimum on the reviewed pages. Variant-specific 300/400-level courses remain part of their major requirements.

residency.unit: percent of hours required for each major or minor at Ferrum
residency.evidence: The current Transfer Credit Policy states that degree recipients must complete at least 25 percent of the hours required for their majors and minors at Ferrum.
The reviewed current catalog pages do not state a separate degree-wide Ferrum-credit minimum; do not convert the major/minor percentage into a degree-wide residency rule.

other_degree_constraints: Transfer credit accepted toward graduation generally requires a C or better and correspondence to Ferrum coursework.
Only credit hours, not transfer grades, enter the Ferrum record for degree progress.

course_dictionary.evidence: Official current catalog Course Descriptions index; variant program course links resolve against catoid 25.

capture_blockers: The stale registry seed poid=3062 is not a neutral base program: it is specifically the Cybersecurity variant. A generic discovery score can also select Network, Programming, or Web Design depending on link order.

No source-backed rule identifies one of the four required emphasis awards as the standard Computer Science B.S.; the program should remain blocked from analysis until the intended variant is chosen explicitly.
No current aggregate college-wide upper-division minimum or separate degree-wide institutional-credit minimum was found.

sources.evidence: Authoritative list of the four separately named Computer Science B.S. variants.
Transfer-credit rules and 25-percent major/minor Ferrum-credit rule.

institutions.name: Radford University

degree.selected_variant: base Computer Science B.S. without a concentration; use the published 12-credit upper-level CS alternative
degree.published_major_credits: 55-88 across the base and concentration choices

owner.college_or_school: Artis College of Science and Technology
owner.department: School of Computing and Information Sciences
owner.evidence: Radford's current official program and school pages place the Computer Science B.S. in the School of Computing and Information Sciences within the Artis College of Science and Technology.

major_requirements.evidence: The catalog page publishes the REAL, school, B.S., computer science, and concentration-or-12-credit base alternative requirements.

exclude_from_base_requirements.content: the five optional concentration requirement blocks
exclude_from_base_requirements.reason: The current catalog explicitly permits four approved upper-level CS courses instead of a concentration; concentration blocks must not be aggregated into the base path.

general_education.published_credits: at least 30 General Education-designated credits within the degree; the integrated REAL framework totals a minimum 48 hours and can include major, minor, and degree work
general_education.evidence: The CS program requires at least 30 credits of GE-designated courses. The REAL authority publishes a 48-hour minimum framework and explains that majors and minors satisfy REAL areas, so 48 must not be modeled as an additional standalone GE block.

total_credits.evidence: Academic Programs General Information and Undergraduate Academic Policies state that no fewer than 120 semester hours are required.

upper_division.evidence: No single university-wide upper-level-credit total is published on the reviewed current policy, REAL, or program pages.

residency.evidence: Current Degree Requirements state that no fewer than 30 bachelor-level credit hours must be earned at Radford to be eligible for graduation.

other_degree_constraints: The Computer Science major fulfills the R and L areas; students must fulfill the E and A REAL areas with majors and/or minors.
Students must complete at least 15 hours, excluding foundational math and writing, outside the department or school housing the first major.
The B.S. requirement contributes 6-8 science credits, with the exact rule depending on the selected base or concentration path.

course_dictionary.evidence: Official current catalog Courses index for catoid 62; program course links resolve into this catalog.

capture_blockers: The 55-88 major-credit range spans mutually exclusive concentration and no-concentration paths. It is not a sum and must not be used as one requirement block.
The REAL 48-hour framework overlaps major/minor/degree work; adding it gross on top of the CS program would double count requirements.

sources.evidence: Current base B.S., optional concentration blocks, and explicit no-concentration alternative.
Current degree completion, institutional-credit, and graduation policies.
